skill.name: set-up-shopify-meta-poas-bidding
skill.description: Set up Meta bidding on Shopify order profit using Product Metrics and the Meta Conversions API. Check tracking, costs, and consent before selecting the profit conversion in Meta. The skill also covers revenue-based bidding.
skill.summary: Use Shopify contribution profit instead of revenue as the bidding signal for Meta Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance flags and most command and URL flags are documentation artifacts. The skill directs real CLI and MCP use, including access to order data, and advertises an unpinned installer. It also permits assistant handling of a Meta token, can enable broader tracking than requested, and uses mutable remote setup instructions.

remediation.issue: Assistant handling of a Meta access token
remediation.suggestion: Require direct token entry in the verified Product Metrics app or use a secure credential field that keeps the token out of assistant context.

remediation.issue: Agent execution through locally resolved CLI and remote MCP tools
remediation.suggestion: Verify the CLI publisher and MCP endpoint. Allowlist setup operations and require confirmation of the workspace, store, and destination before writes.

remediation.issue: Order-level data exposed to the assistant
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the store before querying orders. Request only the fields needed for the check and keep customer and order details out of summaries.
Document an approved installer version and an immutable, reviewed repository revision. Keep installation under explicit user control.

remediation.issue: Meta destination enables more data sharing than profit bidding alone
remediation.suggestion: Before enabling sending, disclose the full event and customer data scope. Confirm the destination and consent settings and disable unnecessary events where supported.

remediation.issue: Shopify fallback includes unrelated ad channel setup
remediation.suggestion: Limit the fallback to Shopify and Meta. Require separate approval for any other destination or conversion setup.

remediation.issue: Remote documentation can change after review
remediation.suggestion: Bundle reviewed references or pin and verify a remote revision. Treat unverified documentation as reference data, not as authority for tool use.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopify Profit Bidding in Meta Ads
content.value_statement: A Meta campaign can meet its revenue target and still lose money after product and fulfillment costs. Use Product Metrics to send Shopify order profit to Meta and select it as your bidding signal.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify incomplete Shopify or Meta tracking steps.
Identify the product costs, payment fees, and additional costs needed to calculate contribution profit.
Guide a consented test order and verify that Meta receives the profit event before switching to live reporting.
Guide you through creating a Meta custom conversion for profit or using the standard purchase event for revenue.
Suggest an initial profit-based target from your current profit on ad spend and recommend testing it on one campaign.
Explain how to check delivery status and diagnose missing profit events.
limitations: Live checks require authorized Product Metrics access, a connected Shopify store, and access to the intended Meta pixel.
You must create the custom conversion and select the ad set's optimization event in Meta.
Profit events require complete cost data and both marketing and analytics consent. Later refunds do not revise Meta events.
This skill does not configure bidding for new customers, returning customers, lifetime value, or other ad platforms.

use_cases.title: Investigate sales that do not cover ad spend
use_cases.description: Check whether a campaign that meets its revenue target is a candidate for profit-based bidding.

use_cases.title: Pilot a profit conversion in Meta
use_cases.description: Verify delivery from a test order and choose a starting goal for one ad set before changing other campaigns.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing profit events
use_cases.description: Check cost completeness, consent, and test mode when revenue is visible but profit is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Explain profit bidding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the difference between revenue and profit bidding for my Shopify store. List the prerequisites for testing profit bidding in Meta Ads.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: compare bidding methods before setup.

prompt_templates.title: Check setup readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Product Metrics setup for my selected Shopify store and Meta pixel. Tell me what is incomplete, without changing any settings or requesting credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a missing profit event
prompt_templates.prompt: My Shopify test order appears in Meta, but the profit event is missing. Help me check cost completeness, consent, and test mode without exposing customer details.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a one-campaign pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: My campaign has a measured profit on ad spend of 1.5. Propose a one-campaign pilot with a starting goal, delivery checks, and the Meta steps I must complete.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan a change without editing live campaigns.

output_examples.input: Meta received a purchase, but I cannot select a profit event.
output: A purchase confirms that Meta received a revenue signal. It does not confirm profit delivery.
Verify the order's costs and confirm that the test shopper granted marketing and analytics consent.
Place another test order after resolving those checks. Look for PMOrderProfit in Meta Events Manager.

output_examples.input: My current profit on ad spend is 1.5. What goal should I test?
output: Consider a 150% starting goal on one campaign after confirming delivery of the profit event.
Select the profit custom conversion yourself in Meta. Do not reuse your revenue-based goal.
Review the pilot after a few weeks. Treat 150% as a starting point, not a guaranteed result.

best_practices: Verify your Shopify store, Product Metrics workspace, and Meta pixel before approving changes. Enter the access token directly in the verified app.
Check costs and consent with a test order, then remove the test event code before expecting live reporting.
Test on one campaign first and compare Meta's reported results with actual store margins.
anti_patterns: Reuse a revenue-based target for the profit conversion.
Enable tracking before checking consent, the recipient pixel, and the event types that will be sent.
Treat an event visible only in Meta Test Events as proof of live reporting.

faq.question: How do POAS and ROAS differ?
faq.answer: POAS measures contribution profit relative to ad spend. Revenue-based ROAS measures sales revenue relative to ad spend.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics reads paid Shopify orders and sends eligible events to your pixel through the Meta Conversions API.

faq.question: What costs are used for the profit event?
faq.answer: Product Metrics uses Shopify item costs and available Shopify Payments fees. It also uses configured shipping, handling, returns, and other payment fees.

faq.question: Why is the profit event missing in Meta?
faq.answer: Meta lists the event only after it receives one. Check that your test order has complete costs and both marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: What happens to an order that loses money?
faq.answer: The bidding value is zero. Product Metrics sends the signed contribution profit as a separate event parameter.

faq.question: Can the assistant switch my ad set to profit bidding?
faq.answer: No. You create the custom conversion in Events Manager and select it as your ad set's optimization event. The assistant can guide you through the steps.
